bug_description.original: Crash Type: Stack-buffer-overflow READ {*} Crash State: nullable_memcpy nsh_key_to_attr parse_odp_push_nsh_action
bug_description.normalized: In parse_odp_push_nsh_action, a crafted push_nsh action with mdtype=2 and an oversized md2 hex field is decoded through a stub-backed ofpbuf that starts on the 248-byte stack array metadata. Decoding 249 MD2 bytes forces the temporary ofpbuf onto heap, but the code later ignores b.data and passes the original stack array together with padded md_size=252 to nsh_key_to_attr. The resulting netlink copy reads 252 bytes from the 248-byte stack object metadata, causing a stack-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant state: the attacker-controlled action text sets nsh.mdtype to NSH_M_TYPE2, which selects the MD2 parsing branch that uses the local metadata stack buffer.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is a NUL-terminated OVS action string `push_nsh(mdtype=2md2=0x<498 hex digits>)\0`. Its `mdtype=2` field is the first vulnerability-relevant state parsed inside project code on the crashing path.

root_cause.description: The parser forwards the original 248-byte stack array `metadata` together with attacker-derived `md_size` into `nsh_key_to_attr`. For the witness, `md_size` is 252 even though the code never substitutes the grown temporary buffer `b.data` or rejects the oversized MD2 payload.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds a size condition on the `md2` parse branch so this `(metadata, md_size)` pair is not formed for the oversized witness.

sink.description: Final crashing read. nullable_memcpy copies n=252 bytes from src=metadata, so memcpy reads 4 bytes past the 248-byte stack array metadata into the redzone.
sink.note: ASan reports `READ of size 252` and identifies `metadata` in parse_odp_push_nsh_action as the over-read stack object, ending at offset 408 in the frame.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled md2 hex field is copied into local buf[512]. In the staged witness it contains 498 hex digits, which decode to 249 bytes before 4-byte padding.

parser_admitted.note: The action parser recognizes the witness string as a push_nsh action and dispatches into parse_odp_push_nsh_action. The witness then parses `mdtype=2` and resumes immediately at `md2=...`, even without a delimiter, because the numeric scan stops at the `m` in `md2`.

coarse_trace.summary: The OSS-Fuzz target passes the staged NUL-terminated action string to odp_actions_from_string for datapath-action parsing.

The push_nsh parser selects MD2 mode, parses an oversized md2 hex payload, decodes 249 bytes through a stub-backed ofpbuf rooted at the 248-byte stack array metadata, derives padded md_size=252, and then forwards the original stack pointer plus that size to nsh_key_to_attr.
The NSH serializer sees metadata != NULL and md_size > 0, calls nl_msg_put_unspec for OVS_NSH_KEY_ATTR_MD2, and the subsequent nullable_memcpy reads 252 bytes from the 248-byte metadata stack object.

fine_trace.note: The witness text sets `nsh.mdtype = 2` (NSH_M_TYPE2). This selects the MD2 metadata branch and resets `md_size` so later MD2 parsing controls the outgoing metadata length.
The attacker-controlled `md2=` field is materialized into `buf[512]`. In the staged PoC, this field holds 498 hex digits, i.e. 249 decoded metadata bytes before padding.

The temporary ofpbuf `b` is initialized to use the 248-byte stack array `metadata` as its backing storage (`NSH_CTX_HDRS_MAX_LEN = 248`). At this point `b.data` aliases the stack object that is later passed to `nsh_key_to_attr`.

The attacker hex string is decoded into `b`. The staged witness yields `mdlen = 249`; appending the 249th byte exhausts the 248-byte stub, so `b` expands to heap-backed storage while `metadata` remains only the original 248-byte stack array.

fine_trace.code: padding = PAD_SIZE(mdlen, 4); if (padding > 0) { ofpbuf_push_zeros(&b, padding); } md_size = mdlen + padding;
fine_trace.note: The decoded MD2 length is rounded up to a 4-byte boundary. For the witness, `padding = 3`, `ofpbuf_push_zeros` grows the temporary buffer to hold that padding, and `md_size` becomes 252.

On the successful parse path, the function forwards the original stack array pointer `metadata` together with `md_size = 252` into `nsh_key_to_attr`. It does not pass the current `b.data`, so the call pairs a 252-byte length with a 248-byte stack object.

fine_trace.code: if (metadata && md_size > 0) { nl_msg_put_unspec(buf, OVS_NSH_KEY_ATTR_MD2, metadata, md_size); }
fine_trace.note: Because `metadata` is non-null and `md_size` is 252, the MD2 serialization branch requests a 252-byte copy from `metadata` into the netlink message.

The netlink helper reaches `nullable_memcpy` with `src = metadata` and `n = 252`, so `memcpy` performs the final 252-byte read from the 248-byte stack array. ASan reports the read starts at the end of the `metadata` object in the parse_odp_push_nsh_action frame.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from the staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json artifacts

poc.trigger: Parsing the staged witness action string through odp_actions_from_string reaches parse_odp_push_nsh_action, decodes 249 MD2 bytes from the `md2=` field, pads them to `md_size = 252`, and then copies 252 bytes from the original 248-byte stack array `metadata`, producing the witnessed ASan stack-buffer-overflow read.

format.name: OVS datapath action string
format.contract: A NUL-terminated single-line action string accepted by the OSS-Fuzz harness, specifically the staged witness form `push_nsh(mdtype=2md2=0x<498 hex digits>)\0`; the `md2` field decodes to 249 bytes and is padded to 252 bytes before serialization, while the local stack array `metadata` is only 248 bytes.
